{"world_model":"W3 (cost lens), after E016. The tip is E016: E015's recipe with weight decay halved to 0.006. That recipe is Muon with 3 Newton-Schulz steps, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps, batch size 2000, widths 128/384/512, label smoothing 0.3, 9.5 epochs (238 steps), compiled in max-autotune with CUDA graphs. It runs in 6.580 s at 0.7607. Note: several idea descriptions say "9 epochs", but the code has 9.5.

Miss: I called the weight-decay change near-noise, and it gave +0.33 pp. Weight decay only reaches the BN biases, whitening bias and head; Muon renormalizes the filters every step. So either the head and bias regularization really matters on CIFAR-100, or this is another ±0.3 pp reshuffle like E015's +0.27. I split it roughly 50/50. I treat about 0.2 pp of the 0.76 pp margin as real.

Time budget: time ≈ F + V × average pixel fraction.
- F is about 0.6-0.9 s (upload, whitening, augmentation, interpolation, permutation).
- V is about 7.5 s at full 32 px.
- The current average pixel fraction is about 0.755 (0.4×0.5625 + 0.3×0.766 + 0.3×1).
- A full-resolution step costs about 30 ms; a 24 px step about 18-20 ms, because smaller maps run less efficiently.
- Host overhead is about 1% (E015), so systems levers are exhausted. The remaining levers are FLOPs (epochs, pixels, width) and F.

Measured prices:
- compile: -14% time (E004).
- Lookahead: about +1 pp at 0 s (E005).
- Muon: +0.66 pp for +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: -22% time for about 0 pp (E007).
- Aggressive resizing that cut the 32 px tail to 20%: 0.9 s/pp, a bad trade (E011). The 32 px tail length looks like the accuracy-critical part.
- Epochs: about 2 s/pp.
- Last-group width: about 1.6 s/pp.
- CUDA graphs: -1% time.
- Hyperparameter nudges (LS 0.2, Muon lr ×1.5, LR decay to 0): all within ±0.1 pp. Weight-decay halving: +0.33 pp (ambiguous).

Mechanisms I believe:
1. Endpoint averaging plus the Lookahead fast-weight reset gives about 1 pp. A plain EMA with a cubic alpha ramp only averages over about the last 20 steps and gives up the reset's smoothing of the trajectory. I expect a 0.2-0.6 pp loss.
2. Accuracy is set mostly in the final 32 px phase, which has the low LR and EMA active. Early low-resolution steps are cheap and are worth less per step, so trimming them, or swapping 28 px for 24 px, is the best remaining time-per-pp trade (about 0.4 s per 0.2-0.4 pp).
3. Group 2 (384 channels at 16×16) is about 45% of conv FLOPs. Narrowing it to 320 cuts about 12% of compute, worth about 0.5 s. CIFAR-100 is width-hungry, so I expect a 0.4-0.8 pp loss.

Noise:
- Per-seed std is 0.2-0.35 pp, so the 3-seed standard error is about 0.17 pp.
- A recipe change reshuffles accuracy by up to ±0.3 pp.
- Compiled runs are bit-reproducible when the same kernels are selected.
- Time noise is about 1%.

Unsure:
- The 40-seed offset of the tip.
- Whether the weight-decay gain is real.
- Whether a fresh max-autotune build reselects the same kernels; if not, results are not bit-reproducible.

structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E016. The tip is E016: E015's recipe with weight decay halved to 0.006. That recipe is Muon with 3 Newton-Schulz steps, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps, batch size 2000, widths 128/384/512, label smoothing 0.3, 9.5 epochs (238 steps), compiled in max-autotune with CUDA graphs. It runs in 6.580 s at 0.7607. Note: several idea descriptions say "9 epochs", but the code has 9.5.

Miss: I called the weight-decay change near-noise, and it gave +0.33 pp. Weight decay only reaches the BN biases, whitening bias and head; Muon renormalizes the filters every step. So either the head and bias regularization really matters on CIFAR-100, or this is another ±0.3 pp reshuffle like E015's +0.27. I split it roughly 50/50. I treat about 0.2 pp of the 0.76 pp margin as real.

Time budget: time ≈ F + V × average pixel fraction.
- F is about 0.6-0.9 s (upload, whitening, augmentation, interpolation, permutation).
- V is about 7.5 s at full 32 px.
- The current average pixel fraction is about 0.755 (0.4×0.5625 + 0.3×0.766 + 0.3×1).
- A full-resolution step costs about 30 ms; a 24 px step about 18-20 ms, because smaller maps run less efficiently.
- Host overhead is about 1% (E015), so systems levers are exhausted. The remaining levers are FLOPs (epochs, pixels, width) and F.

Measured prices:
- compile: -14% time (E004).
- Lookahead: about +1 pp at 0 s (E005).
- Muon: +0.66 pp for +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: -22% time for about 0 pp (E007).
- Aggressive resizing that cut the 32 px tail to 20%: 0.9 s/pp, a bad trade (E011). The 32 px tail length looks like the accuracy-critical part.
- Epochs: about 2 s/pp.
- Last-group width: about 1.6 s/pp.
- CUDA graphs: -1% time.
- Hyperparameter nudges (LS 0.2, Muon lr ×1.5, LR decay to 0): all within ±0.1 pp. Weight-decay halving: +0.33 pp (ambiguous).

Mechanisms I believe:
1. Endpoint averaging plus the Lookahead fast-weight reset gives about 1 pp. A plain EMA with a cubic alpha ramp only averages over about the last 20 steps and gives up the reset's smoothing of the trajectory. I expect a 0.2-0.6 pp loss.
2. Accuracy is set mostly in the final 32 px phase, which has the low LR and EMA active. Early low-resolution steps are cheap and are worth less per step, so trimming them, or swapping 28 px for 24 px, is the best remaining time-per-pp trade (about 0.4 s per 0.2-0.4 pp).
3. Group 2 (384 channels at 16×16) is about 45% of conv FLOPs. Narrowing it to 320 cuts about 12% of compute, worth about 0.5 s. CIFAR-100 is width-hungry, so I expect a 0.4-0.8 pp loss.

Noise:
- Per-seed std is 0.2-0.35 pp, so the 3-seed standard error is about 0.17 pp.
- A recipe change reshuffles accuracy by up to ±0.3 pp.
- Compiled runs are bit-reproducible when the same kernels are selected.
- Time noise is about 1%.

Unsure:
- The 40-seed offset of the tip.
- Whether the weight-decay gain is real.
- Whether a fresh max-autotune build reselects the same kernels; if not, results are not bit-reproducible.
- The real per-step cost at 24 px compared with 28 px.

forecasts.reason: A plain EMA with a cubic ramp loses Lookahead's fast-weight reset; I expect it 0.2-0.6 pp below the tip at the same cost.
30% of steps go from 28 to 24 px, a pixel saving of about 0.06 × V ≈ 0.35-0.45 s. The 32 px tail is untouched, so the loss should be small.
About 19 fewer 24 px steps saves about 0.35 s. Stretching the schedules shifts the LR shape slightly; the loss of about 0.3 pp is within noise of the 0.3 pp/0.5-epoch claim.
No recipe change. Max-autotune most likely reselects the same kernels, giving bit-identical per-seed accuracy and time within 2%.
Optimizer nudges have all been within ±0.1 pp apart from weight decay. Momentum 0.8 is unlikely to add 0.3 pp and could cost a little.
About 12% fewer conv FLOPs saves about 0.5 s, but CIFAR-100 is width-sensitive (E010 lost 0.43 pp). The loss of about 0.6 pp would threaten the 0.753 bar.

cruxes: Is E016's +0.33 pp from halving weight decay real, or a reshuffle? Held-out seeds 3-12 would decide how much margin can be spent on cutting epochs or pixels.
What does a 24 px step cost compared with a 28 px or 32 px step (CUDA-event timing)? This sets the true savings of I023 and I024 against the width cut in I028.

How much of the 6.58 s is the fixed cost F (upload, whitening, per-epoch augmentation, interpolation) rather than steps? If F is over 1 s, moving augmentation into the compiled graph becomes a lever again.
